newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo trade minister calls for VAT law - papers.
newsitem.headline: Yugo trade minister calls for VAT law - papers.

text.p: The Yugoslav trade minister has called for the introduction of a law on value added tax as soon as possible to unify tax regulations and attract foreign investors, Belgrade newspapers reported on Monday.

"Such a tax system is in force in all European Union states. It enables foreigners to determine exactly how much they have earned and the net profit they can transfer," Borislav Vukovic was quoted by Politika Ekspres daily as saying.
Vukovic said foreigners fxavoured stability in the economic environment and simplified administrative procedures.
He said production could not be triggered by domestic demand due to the low purchasing power of the population, but rather through demand for Yugoslav exports.

Vukovic said there would be a further liberalisation of exports but that restrictions would remain for strategic agricultural products such as wheat, maize, meat, livestock, flour, sugar and table oil to ensure stable supply of food.
Regulations protecting domestic production from dumping prices and illegal subsidies are expected to be passed at the end of July, Vukovic said.
But he added more balanced foreign trade could not be achieved by reducing imports.

"Imports must grow, as our economy needs raw materials and semi-finished goods, spare parts and equipment, so the only way out is faster growth of exports," Vukovic said. -- Beti Bilandzic, Belgrade newsroom +381 11 222 4305
